questions.question: Chlorine, bromine and iodine make a Dobereiner's triad. The average of atomic masses of chlorine and Iodine would be close to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**79.9.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Dobereiner's triad **is a group of **three elements **with **similar properties**.
 
• In this case, the triad consists of **chlorine, bromine, and iodine**.
 
• According to Dobereiner's law of triads, the **atomic mass** of the **middle element** is the **average** of the atomic masses of the other two.
 
• Therefore, the atomic mass of bromine should be **close **to the** average** of the atomic masses of chlorine and iodine.
 
• The atomic mass of chlorine is **35.5 **and the atomic mass of iodine is **126.9.**
 
• Therefore, the average of these two values is (35.5 + 126.9) / 2 = **81.2**.
 
• This value is closest to option 3, which is **79.9.**
 
• Chlorine, bromine, and iodine are **halogens**, which are **highly reactive nonmetals.**
 
• They all have **seven valence electrons** and tend to form salts with metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorine** has an atomic number of **17 **and the symbol Cl.

 
 
• Among the halogens, it is the **second-lightest.**
 
 
 
• Atomic number** 35** and symbol Br belong to** bromine**.
 
 
• When it is at room temperature, it is a** volatile reddish-brown** liquid.
 
 
 
• **Iodine **has an atomic number of **53** and the symbol** I.**
 
 
• Of the **stable halogens,** it is the heaviest.
 
 
 
• With valence shell **d orbitals**, chlorine, bromine, and iodine can expand their valence shells to include up to **14 valence electrons.**

questions.question: Corrosion is a type of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**oxidation reaction.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Corrosion** is a type of **oxidation reaction.**
 
• Corrosion is a process of** gradual destruction or deterioration** of metals due to chemical reactions with their environment.
 
• This process involves the** loss of electrons** from metal atoms, which is known as** oxidation.**
 
• During corrosion, metal atoms lose electrons and form **positive ions**, which combine with **negative ions** from the environment to form **corrosion products** such as **rust, tarnish, or patina.**
 
• Corrosion can occur in various forms such as** uniform corrosion, pitting corrosion, galvanic corrosion, and crevice corrosion.**
 
• Each type of corrosion has its own specific mechanism and can be influenced by factors such as **temperature, humidity, pH, and presence of corrosive agents.**
 
• Corrosion can be prevented or minimized by various methods such as **surface coatings, cathodic protection, alloying, and proper design** and maintenance of structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction in which** one element or ion displaces** another element or ion from a compound.

 
 
• For example, when zinc metal is added to hydrochloric acid, **hydrogen gas** is evolved and** zinc chloride** is formed.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition reaction **is a type of chemical reaction in which a compound breaks down into** simpler compounds** or elements.
 
 
• For example, when calcium carbonate is heated, it decomposes into **calcium oxide** and **carbon dioxide.**
 
 
 
• **Double displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction in which two compounds **exchange ions** to form two new compounds.
 
 
• For example, when sodium chloride is mixed with silver nitrate, **silver chloride and sodium nitrate** are formed.

questions.question:
Which of the following measures is/are likely to be adopted by RBI to combat inflation?

A) Increase CRR.

(B) Increase Repo Rate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increase CRR:**

 
 
• This is a measure to **reduce the liquidity** in the market by **increasing the percentage of deposits **that banks have to keep with the RBI.
 
• This **reduces the amount of money **available for lending and thereby** reduces inflationary pressure.**
 
 
 
• **Increase Repo Rate: **
 
 
• This is a measure to** increase the cost of borrowing **for banks, which in turn** increases the cost of lending** for customers.
 
• This **reduces the demand for loans** and thereby reduces inflationary pressure.
 
 
 
• **CRR** stands for Cash Reserve Ratio, which is the **percentage of deposits** that banks have to keep with the RBI.
 
• **Repo Rate** is the rate at which the RBI l**ends money to commercial banks** for short periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other measures **that RBI may adopt to combat inflation include:
 
• **Open market operations:**
 
 
• **​**RBI can sell government securities in the open market to **reduce the money supply** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Increase in bank rate: **
 
 
• **​**This is the rate at which** RBI lends to commercial banks**.
 
• An increase in this rate **increases the cost of borrowing for banks** and reduces the money supply in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal measures:**
 
 
• **​**The government can** increase taxes or reduce spending** to reduce the demand for goods and services, thereby reducing inflationary pressure.

questions.question: Three wires, A, B and C, of the same length and the same thickness have resistances of 0.5 Ω, 0.2 Ω and 1.0 Ω, respectively. Their resistivities are ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** in the ratio of 5 ∶ 2 ∶ 10.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **resistivity **of a material is defined as the** resistance** of a **unit length **of the material having **unit cross-sectional area.**
 
• Therefore, resistivity is **directly proportional **to resistance and** inversely proportional **to the length of the wire.
 
• The given wires are of the** same length and thickness,** but their resistances are **different.**
 
• This means that their **resistivities** are **different **as well.
 
• To find the ratio of their resistivities, we can use the formula: **Resistance = (Resistivity x Length) / Cross-sectional area.**
 
• Since the length and cross-sectional area are the same for all wires, we can directly compare their resistances to find the **ratio of their resistivities.**
 
• From the given resistances, we can see that wire **B has the lowest resistance,** which means it has the** highest conductivity and lowest resistivity.**
 
• Therefore, **"in the ratio of 5:2:10"** is the correct answer as it correctly represents the increasing order of resistivity of **wires A, B, and C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity** is a fundamental property of a material that determines its ability to **conduct electricity.**
 
• It is denoted by the Greek letter** rho** and its unit is **ohm-meter.**
 
• The resistivity of a material depends on various factors such as **temperature, impurities, and crystal structure.**
 
• Metals have **low resistivity** and are** good conductors **of electricity, while insulators have **high resistivity **and are **poor conductors **of electricity.
 
• The resistance of a wire also depends on its **length and cross-sectional area,** in addition to its resistivity.
 
 
• The **longer **the wire, the **higher** its resistance, and the** wider **the wire, the** lower** its resistance.
 
• In general, the resistance of a wire can be reduced by** increasing its thickness** or by using a material with higher conductivity (lower resistivity).
 
 
 
• This is why copper wires are commonly used in** electrical wiring **as they have **low resistivity** and are relatively inexpensive.

questions.question: A cistern has three pipes A, B and C. A and B alone can completely fill the cistern in 4 hours and 3 hours, respectively, and C can empty the completely filled cistern in 2 hours. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously in the empty cistern, then the cistern will get completely full in:
questions.solution:
Given:

A and B alone can completely fill the cistern in 4 hours and 3 hours, respectively, and C can empty the completely filled cistern in 2 hours

Concept used:

Efficiency × Time = Work

Calculation:

Total work = LCM(4, 3 and 2 hours) = 12 

 

A's efficiency = 12/4 = 3

B's efficiency = 12/3 = 4

C's efficiency = 12/2 = 6

(A + B + (-C)) = 4 + 3 - 6 = 1

Time to fill tank together = 12/1 = 12 hours.

**The answer is 12 hours.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the process of excretion in plants?

options.text: Waste products may be stored as resins and gums in old xylem.
Waste products may be stored in leaves that fall off.
Waste product of photosynthesis is stored as starch.
Waste products are stored in cellular vacuoles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waste product of photosynthesis is stored as starch.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of **excretion in plants** involves the **removal of waste products** that are produced during various **metabolic activities. **
 
• "Waste product of photosynthesis is stored as starch." statement is** incorrect.** 
 
• The waste product of photosynthesis is oxygen, while the** excess glucose** produced during the process is **stored as starch.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Resins and gums** are waste products that are stored in the** old xylem **of some plants.

 
 
• These substances are often used for** defense against predators **or as a means of sealing wounds.
 
 
 
• Some plants store waste products in the **leaves that fall off** during the autumn season.
 
 
• This helps to **conserve resources** and maintain the **overall health **of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Cellular vacuoles** are storage spaces in plants that can store various waste products, such as **excess salts, pigments, and metabolic byproducts**.
 
 
• These vacuoles also play a crucial role in maintaining** turgor pressure** and **regulating the pH of the cell.**

questions.question: The measure of responsiveness of the demand for Tea towards the change in the price of Coffee in the market is an example of ________.

__
 
• **Cross Elasticity of Demand** is a measure that determines how the demand for **one product changes** in response to a **change in the price **of a different product.
 
• It is calculated by dividing the **percentage change** in the quantity demanded of one product by the percentage change in the **price of another** product.
 
• Therefore, the measure of responsiveness of the** demand for Tea** towards the change in the** price of Coffee** in the market is an example of Cross Elasticity of Demand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composite Demand r**efers to the** demand for a product** that is used in conjunction with another product.

 
 
• For example, the **demand for petrol** is a composite demand as it is used in conjunction with automobiles.
 
 
 
• **Indirect Demand** refers to the demand for a product that is derived from the **demand of another product**.
 
 
• For example, the **demand for car tires** is an indirect demand as it is derived from the demand for automobiles.
 
 
 
• **Direct Demand** refers to the demand for a product that is **not related **to the demand for any other product.

questions.question: When there are two houses of the legislature like India, it is called a _____ legislature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bicameral.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **bicameral legislature** is one that has **two separate chambers **or houses of parliament, each with its own set of **elected representatives.**
 
• **India's parliament** is a bicameral legislature, with the **Rajya Sabha **(Council of States) as the** upper house** and the **Lok Sabha** (House of the People) as the** lower house.**
 
• The purpose of having two houses in a bicameral legislature is to provide a system of** checks and balances, **ensuring that no single house has too much power and that legislation is carefully **considered and debated **before being passed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unicameral legislatures**, on the other hand, have only **one house of parliament**, which can sometimes lead to a lack of diverse perspectives and less thorough debate and scrutiny of proposed laws.

 
 
• Unicameral legislatures are more common in** smaller countries** or those with a** unitary system of government**, where there is less need for multiple chambers to represent different regions or interest groups.
 
• Some countries, such as the **United States,** have a bicameral legislature at the **federal **level but a unicameral legislature at the **state level.**
 
 
 
• **Subordinate legislatures,** also known as subordinate authorities or subordinate parliaments, are those that have** limited powers** and are subject to the authority of a **higher-level parliament or government.**
 
• **Supreme legislatures, **on the other hand, are those that have ultimate authority over all other branches of government and can** overrule or veto** any decisions made by lower bodies.
 
 
• However, this type of system is** rare **and is usually associated with** authoritarian regimes **rather than democratic ones.

questions.question: Which of the following optical phenomena can explain the visibility of the sun, two minutes prior to actual sunrise?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric Refraction.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric refraction** is the** bending of light **that occurs when it passes through the** Earth's atmosphere.**
 
• It is caused due to the **variation in the refractive index** of the atmosphere with altitude.
 
• This bending of light is responsible for the **visibility of the sun,** two minutes prior to actual sunrise.
 
• The Earth's atmosphere acts as a lens and** refracts the sunlight towards the observer**, even when the sun is below the horizon.
 
• This causes the sun to appear higher in the sky than it actually is, giving the impression that the** sun has risen.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersion of light** is the** separation of white light** into its constituent colors when it passes through a prism.

options.text: Amount of dissolved waste to be excreted

__
 
• The** amount of filtrate reabsorbed** depends on the amount of **excess water **and the amount of **dissolved waste** to be excreted.
 
• This means that if there is **more excess** water in the body, the kidneys will **reabsorb less filtrate** and **excrete more urine.**
 
• Similarly, if there is **more dissolved waste **in the body, the kidneys will reabsorb** less filtrate** and** excrete more urine.**
 
• The reabsorption of filtrate is controlled by the hormones** aldosterone and antidiuretic hormone** (ADH).
 
• These hormones regulate the **amount of water and sodium** that is reabsorbed by the kidneys, which in turn affects the amount of filtrate that is excreted as urine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Other factors that can affect the amount of filtrate reabsorbed include** blood pressure, blood pH,** and the **concentration of electrolytes **in the blood.
 
• The main keyword in the question is "filtrate," which refers to the fluid that is** filtered from the blood **by the kidneys.
 
• This fluid contains** water, waste products, and other substances **that need to be either reabsorbed or excreted as urine.

**Formula used:**

Median = L + [(N/2 - CF)/f] × w

f = Frequency of median class

w = Width of median class

**Calculation:**

Total frequency (N) = 22 + 18 + 25 + 15 + 20 = 100

questions.question: The Lok Sabha passed the Family Courts' Amendment Bill in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**July 2022.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Family Courts' Amendment Bill **seeks to amend the** Family Courts Act, 1984**, which provides for the establishment of **family courts **for speedy settlement of disputes relating to **marriage and family affairs.**
 
• The **Lok Sabha**, the lower house of the Indian Parliament, passed the Bill in **July 2022**, which means that it has been **approved **by the elected representatives of the people.
 
• The Bill proposes several amendments to the original Act, including the provision for **digital recording of evidence **and the establishment of **counselling centres** to help parties resolve their disputes amicably.
 
• The Bill also seeks to improve the** functioning of family courts** by providing for the appointment of **more judges and support staff,** and by enabling the** transfer of cases **between courts for better case management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The purpose of the Family Courts (Amendment) Bill is to establish Family Courts in the states of **Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland**, respectively, beginning on **February 15, 2019, **and **September 12, 2008.**
 
• In order to retrospectively recognize all actions performed under the aforementioned Act by the State Governments of Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland, as well as the** Family Courts **of both states, prior to the Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 2022, it also aims to incorporate a new **Section 3A.**
 
• The bill states that any** family court judge appointment orders, **as well as any **posting, promotion, or transfer** of such judges pursuant to the Act, will be enforceable in the two States.
